Quote sources

Simone de Beauvoir quote sources

9 passages attributed to Simone de Beauvoir in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Beauvoir.

Quote source / Simone de Beauvoir

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

Sourcing profile

Language of the works
French
Cited here from
The Second Sex (1949), in the introduction and both volumes, and The Ethics of Ambiguity (1947).
How to cite it
Name which English edition you are quoting. The two standard ones do not contain the same text, so a citation that gives only “The Second Sex” is ambiguous between them.
Where quotations of this author go wrong
The 1953 English translation by H. M. Parshley was heavily abridged and its cuts were not marked, and a full translation by Borde and Malovany-Chevallier followed in 2009. For six decades English readers quoted Beauvoir from a text that had lost a substantial portion of her argument, and the two editions differ in wording as well. A quotation cannot be checked without knowing which one it came from.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I check quotations attributed to Simone de Beauvoir?

Name which English edition you are quoting. The two standard ones do not contain the same text, so a citation that gives only “The Second Sex” is ambiguous between them. This archive cites Simone de Beauvoir from The Second Sex (1949), in the introduction and both volumes, and The Ethics of Ambiguity (1947). Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

What is the most common mistake when quoting Simone de Beauvoir?

The 1953 English translation by H. M. Parshley was heavily abridged and its cuts were not marked, and a full translation by Borde and Malovany-Chevallier followed in 2009. For six decades English readers quoted Beauvoir from a text that had lost a substantial portion of her argument, and the two editions differ in wording as well. A quotation cannot be checked without knowing which one it came from.

What language did Simone de Beauvoir write in?

French. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
